editorial.brief: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive, and five separate feeds noticed: Wikipedia, Hacker News at 3,273 points, Lemmy, Polymarket and the AI news wire. Elsewhere, Mastodon joked about a Microsoft outage, and the largest of 25 quakes, an M5.8, struck near Kavieng, Papua New Guinea.
editorial.cover_sub: Jensen Huang took 1,072,168 views, a lead of 1.5 times over the second-placed Ramayana: Part 1, on the day Hacker News, Lemmy, Polymarket and the AI wire all reported his resignation from Nvidia.
editorial.wiki_deck: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive, and readers went to check. Wikipedia counted 1,072,168 views for him, well clear of every other article in the snapshot.
editorial.letter_headline: One resignation, while the web carried on
editorial.discourse_deck: Hacker News is gripped by a resignation, Lemmy irritated by a throttled internet plan, Bluesky drifting between poetry and a broken-record quip, Mastodon amused by a Microsoft outage.
editorial.foreign_deck: Nvidia's CEO exit and a potential record Anthropic IPO drawing orders for six times the shares available led the wire, while searchers in Britain, India and the United States typed afg vs zim.
editorial.markets_deck: At $1M each, two markets sit at 1%, Jesus returning and a December Fed cut; the rest are sport, from UFC 334 at 35% to Vitality vs MOUZ at 56%.
editorial.watch_deck: Counter-Strike 2 peaked at 1,122,168 players on Steam, ahead of Dota 2 at 729,589 and PUBG at 718,335. On Twitch, caseoh_ leads with 65,298 viewers, and Vitality meet MOUZ in the BLAST Rivals playoffs.
editorial.yt_note: Gatto leads at 1,788,834 views, under 10,500 clear of The Weeknd's Hong Kong video. Sonic's 35th anniversary animation and a Darktide class reveal fill the middle; FattMack trails with 72,783.
editorial.closing_note: By tomorrow's edition the Nvidia succession will have either an answer or a new rumour, and 3,273 points on Hacker News will be history. The Microsoft outage jokes will expire, and the M5.8 near Kavieng will be one more line in the quake log.
wiki_paras: Jensen Huang topped Wikipedia with 1,072,168 views. The explanation is not hidden. Hacker News, Lemmy and the AI news wire all carried the same headline: he has resigned as Nvidia chief executive, effective immediately according to the Lemmy post. Readers did what readers do and looked up the man.

The margin was real but not enormous. Ramayana: Part 1 took second place with 735,438 views, so the leader finished at 1.5 times its total. Colette Kress sits third with 463,931 and Nvidia itself fifth with 366,417. Whether Kress is here for the same reason, the data does not say, though the timing is suggestive.

Anthony Clark, the actor, sits fourth with 374,893 views and has no visible link to anything else in the snapshot. Ramayana: Part 1 is equally unexplained by the other feeds. Much of the day's reading was one story. U.S. stocks lost steam on it, the wire says, and the encyclopedia filled up as well.
letter_paras: A single-story day, with a loud middle. Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia appears in five feeds at once, and Hacker News gave it 3,273 points, nearly six times the next story, Rust 1.100 at 570. Around it the snapshot is orderly: 25 quakes of M2.5 or above, the largest an M5.8, and no other topic with comparable reach.

The small print is better. A Lemmy thread reports that New York says T-Mobile imposed a 50GB cap on a low-income home plan and then slowed it to 600Kbps. Hacker News found room for Switcher (2004) at 71 points and IceWM at 41. Mastodon, meanwhile, spent the morning joking about a Microsoft outage to colleagues who did not laugh.

A snapshot taken in one minute across 17 feeds cannot say what mattered. It can say what was loud together, which a daily average blurs. Taken at the same hour each day, the pictures also become comparable: today's 3,273 points can be set against yesterday's edition, and the margin means something.

brief: Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia chief executive, and five separate feeds noticed: Wikipedia, Hacker News at 3,273 points, Lemmy, Polymarket and the AI news wire. Elsewhere, Mastodon joked about a Microsoft outage, and the largest of 25 quakes, an M5.8, struck near Kavieng, Papua New Guinea.
